subject: Biology SL
title: Biology SL Paper 2 Section A Mock v3

questions.subject: Biology SL
questions.question: Answer all parts about DNA composition and replication.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: A double-stranded DNA sample contains 18% guanine. Calculate the expected percentages of cytosine and adenine.
markscheme: Cytosine is 18% because guanine pairs with cytosine.
G + C = 36%, leaving 64% for A + T; adenine is therefore 32%.
markschemeJa: グアニンとシトシンは対になるため、シトシンは18%。
G+C＝36%なのでA+Tは64%、したがってアデニンは32%。
parts.modelAnswerJa: シトシン18%、アデニン32%です。

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Explain how complementary base pairing contributes to accurate DNA replication.
markscheme: Each parental strand acts as a template, and exposed bases pair specifically with complementary nucleotides.
A pairs with T and C pairs with G, so the nucleotide sequence of each new strand is determined by the template sequence.
markschemeJa: 各親鎖が鋳型となり、露出した塩基に相補的ヌクレオチドが特異的に結合する。
AはT、CはGと対合するため、新生鎖の塩基配列は鋳型配列によって決まる。
parts.modelAnswer: Each parental strand is a template. Specific A–T and C–G pairing determines the sequence of the new complementary strand.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 各親鎖が鋳型となり、A-T、C-Gの特異的な対合によって新しい相補鎖の配列が決まります。

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Explain why DNA replication is described as semi-conservative.
markscheme: The two parental DNA strands separate before new complementary strands are synthesized.
Each daughter DNA molecule contains one parental strand and one newly synthesized strand.
markschemeJa: 親DNAの2本鎖が分離してから新しい相補鎖が合成される。
複製後の各DNA分子は親由来の鎖1本と新生鎖1本を含む。
parts.modelAnswer: The parental strands separate and each templates a new strand, so each daughter molecule contains one old strand and one new strand.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 親鎖が分かれてそれぞれ新生鎖の鋳型となるため、各娘DNAは親鎖1本と新生鎖1本を含みます。

questions.subject: Biology SL
questions.question: Scientists compared a homologous DNA region in four closely related animal populations.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Identify the pair with the fewest nucleotide differences.
markscheme: Populations P and Q, with 9 nucleotide differences.
markschemeJa: 塩基差が9で最も少ないPとQ。

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: The homologous region is 900 nucleotides long. Calculate the percentage of nucleotide positions that differ between populations P and Q.
markscheme: Percentage difference = 9 ÷ 900 × 100.
The percentage difference is 1.0%.
markschemeJa: 差の割合は9÷900×100で計算する。
塩基差の割合は1.0%。

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Evaluate the conclusion that populations P and Q must belong to the same species because they have the fewest DNA differences.
markscheme: The small number of sequence differences supports the inference that P and Q are relatively closely related and may share a more recent common ancestor than the other pairs.

A single homologous DNA region does not by itself demonstrate that two populations are the same species because closely related species can have similar sequences and variation can also occur within a species.
Additional evidence such as reproductive compatibility, morphology, ecology and data from multiple independent genes or whole genomes would strengthen a species-level conclusion.
markschemeJa: 塩基差が少ないことは、PとQが比較的近縁で、他の組より最近の共通祖先をもつ可能性を支持する。
1つの相同DNA領域だけでは同種であることを証明できない。近縁な別種でも配列が似ることがあり、同一種内にも変異がある。
生殖的適合性、形態、生態、複数の独立遺伝子や全ゲノムなど追加証拠を組み合わせると、種判定の結論が強くなる。
parts.modelAnswer: P and Q are the closest pair in this DNA dataset, which supports a relatively recent common ancestry. However, similarity in one DNA region does not prove that they are the same species. Species decisions should also consider reproductive, morphological and ecological evidence and preferably multiple independent genetic regions.
parts.modelAnswerJa: このDNAデータではPとQが最も近く、比較的最近の共通祖先をもつことを支持します。しかし1つのDNA領域が似ているだけでは同種とは証明できません。生殖、形態、生態、複数の独立した遺伝領域などの証拠も組み合わせる必要があります。

stimulus.title: Nucleotide differences in the same 900-base DNA region
stimulus.note: All comparisons use the same homologous DNA region.

questions.subject: Biology SL
questions.question: A membrane transport protein was studied at increasing external solute concentration.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Describe the relationship between external solute concentration and transport rate.
markscheme: Transport rate increases as external solute concentration rises at low to moderate concentrations.
At high concentrations the increase becomes smaller and the rate approaches a maximum/plateau.
markschemeJa: 低〜中濃度では外部溶質濃度が上がると輸送速度が増える。
高濃度では増加幅が小さくなり、最大値・頭打ちに近づく。
parts.modelAnswer: The transport rate rises at first and then approaches a plateau as external solute concentration increases.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 輸送速度は最初は増加しますが、外部溶質濃度が高くなると頭打ちに近づきます。

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Explain why a transport protein can show a maximum transport rate.
markscheme: There is a finite number of transport proteins / binding sites in the membrane.
At high solute concentration most transport proteins are occupied or cycling near their maximum rate, so additional solute has little effect.
markschemeJa: 膜中の輸送タンパク質・結合部位の数には限りがある。
高い溶質濃度では多くの輸送タンパク質が占有され最大速度近くで働くため、さらに溶質を増やしても影響が小さい。
parts.modelAnswer: There are only a finite number of transport proteins. At high concentration they become saturated, so further solute has little effect on the maximum rate.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 輸送タンパク質の数には限りがあり、高濃度では飽和するため、さらに溶質を増やしても最大速度はほとんど上がりません。

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Predict how a non-competitive inhibitor that reduces the number of functioning transport proteins would alter the graph.
markscheme: The maximum transport rate would decrease because fewer functional transport proteins are available.
At a given moderate/high solute concentration, transport rate would be lower, while increasing solute could not fully restore the original maximum.
markschemeJa: 機能する輸送タンパク質が減るため最大輸送速度が低下する。
中〜高濃度での輸送速度は低くなり、溶質濃度を上げても元の最大値には完全には戻らない。
parts.modelAnswer: The plateau would be lower because fewer functional proteins are available; adding more solute would not restore the original maximum rate.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 機能する輸送タンパク質が少なくなるため頭打ちの値が低下し、溶質を増やしても元の最大速度には戻りません。

stimulus.title: Solute concentration and membrane transport rate

questions.subject: Biology SL
questions.question: Physiological measurements were recorded during exercise and recovery.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Calculate the percentage increase in cardiac output from rest to intense exercise.

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Explain why ventilation rate and cardiac output increase during intense exercise.
markscheme: Working muscles require more ATP, increasing the rate of cellular respiration.
Higher ventilation increases oxygen uptake and carbon dioxide removal at the lungs.
Higher cardiac output delivers more oxygen/substrates to muscles and transports carbon dioxide and heat away more rapidly.
markschemeJa: 活動筋ではATP需要が増え、細胞呼吸速度が上がる。
換気量増加により肺での酸素取り込みと二酸化炭素排出が増える。
心拍出量増加により筋へ酸素・基質を多く届け、二酸化炭素や熱をより速く運び去る。
parts.modelAnswer: Muscles need more ATP, so respiration increases. Ventilation raises gas exchange, while higher cardiac output delivers oxygen and removes carbon dioxide and heat more quickly.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 筋肉のATP需要が増えて呼吸が活発になります。換気量増加でガス交換を高め、心拍出量増加で酸素供給と二酸化炭素・熱の除去を速めます。

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Explain why ventilation and cardiac output remain above resting values during early recovery.
markscheme: Oxygen is still required to support recovery processes and restore physiological conditions after exercise.
Carbon dioxide, heat and metabolic products still need to be transported and removed while ATP/oxygen stores and homeostasis are restored.
markschemeJa: 運動後の回復過程と生理状態の回復には引き続き酸素が必要である。
ATP・酸素貯蔵や恒常性を回復する間も、二酸化炭素、熱、代謝産物を運び除去する必要がある。
parts.modelAnswer: Recovery still requires oxygen and transport to restore homeostasis and remove carbon dioxide, heat and metabolic products.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 回復中も恒常性を戻し、二酸化炭素・熱・代謝産物を除去するため酸素供給と循環が必要です。

questions.subject: Biology SL
questions.question: Two insect populations experienced different environments over 20 generations.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Describe the change in allele X frequency in the dry environment.
markscheme: Allele X frequency increases steadily from 0.12 at generation 0 to 0.76 at generation 20.
The increase becomes substantial over successive generations rather than occurring as a single-step change.
markschemeJa: 乾燥環境ではXの頻度が世代0の0.12から世代20の0.76まで継続的に増加する。
変化は一度に起こるのではなく、複数世代にわたり大きくなる。
parts.modelAnswer: Allele X rises steadily from 0.12 to 0.76 across 20 generations.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 対立遺伝子Xは20世代で0.12から0.76へ継続的に増加します。

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Compare the allele-frequency pattern in the dry and moist environments.
markscheme: Allele X rises strongly in the dry environment but remains close to the starting frequency in the moist environment.
markschemeJa: Xは乾燥環境で大きく増えるが、湿潤環境では開始頻度付近にとどまる。
parts.modelAnswer: X increases strongly in the dry environment but changes little in the moist environment.
parts.modelAnswerJa: Xは乾燥環境では大きく増えますが、湿潤環境ではほとんど変化しません。

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Explain how natural selection could produce the observed difference between environments.
markscheme: If allele X increases survival or reproductive success in the dry environment, carriers contribute more offspring to the next generation.
Because the advantage depends on environment, the selection pressure may be weak or absent in the moist environment, so allele frequency changes little there.
markschemeJa: Xが乾燥環境で生存・繁殖成功を高めるなら、保有個体が次世代へより多くの子孫を残す。
利点が環境依存なら湿潤環境では選択圧が弱い・ないため、頻度はほとんど変化しない。
parts.modelAnswer: If X improves fitness in dry conditions, carriers leave more offspring and X becomes more common. If it gives little advantage in moist conditions, its frequency changes much less there.
parts.modelAnswerJa: Xが乾燥条件で適応度を高めれば保有個体がより多く繁殖し、Xが増えます。湿潤条件で利点が小さければ頻度変化も小さくなります。

questions.subject: Biology SL
questions.question: Expression of three genes was measured in two specialized cell types from the same organism.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Identify the gene with the largest difference in expression between the two cell types.
markscheme: Gene K.
markschemeJa: 遺伝子K。

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Explain how different gene-expression patterns can lead to specialized cell structure and function.
markscheme: Different genes being expressed cause different proteins to be produced in the two cell types.
Different proteins alter structures, organelle abundance, membrane properties and metabolic activities, producing different specialized functions.
markschemeJa: 異なる遺伝子が発現することで、2つの細胞型で異なるタンパク質がつくられる。
異なるタンパク質が構造、オルガネラ量、膜特性、代謝活動を変え、異なる特殊化機能を生じる。
parts.modelAnswer: Different expression patterns produce different proteins, which determine cell structures and biochemical activities suited to different functions.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 異なる発現パターンによって異なるタンパク質がつくられ、それが細胞構造や生化学的活動を変えて異なる機能に適応させます。

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Explain why the two cell types can have very different expression patterns even though they contain the same genome.
markscheme: Most somatic cells contain the same genes, but regulatory mechanisms activate or suppress different genes in different cell types.
Cell differentiation establishes and maintains these different patterns of gene expression.
markschemeJa: 多くの体細胞は同じ遺伝子をもつが、調節機構により細胞型ごとに異なる遺伝子が活性化・抑制される。
細胞分化によってこれらの異なる遺伝子発現パターンが形成・維持される。
parts.modelAnswer: They share the same genome, but regulation during differentiation turns different genes on or off in each cell type.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 同じゲノムを持っていても、分化過程の調節によって細胞型ごとに異なる遺伝子がオン・オフになります。
